subject: science
notes: When a drop of water lands on a pan only slightly hotter than water's boiling point, it spreads out and boils away within seconds.
On a much hotter pan, above roughly 200 °C, a drop can instead skitter across the surface and last for a minute or more.
This is called the Leidenfrost effect, after the German doctor Johann Gottlob Leidenfrost, who described it in 1756.
At such temperatures, the underside of the drop vaporizes at once, forming a thin cushion of steam.
The steam layer conducts heat poorly, so it slows the transfer of heat from the pan to the drop.
stem: The student wants to contrast the behavior of water drops on moderately hot and very hot pans and explain the difference. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: A drop that boils away in seconds on a moderately hot pan can last a minute on a much hotter one, where a poorly conducting steam cushion forms beneath it.
choices.B: Whereas a water drop boils away within seconds on a pan just above water's boiling point, it can last a minute or more on a much hotter pan.
choices.C: Water drops that last longer on very hot pans are an example of the Leidenfrost effect, named for a German doctor who described it in 1756.
choices.D: A drop of water on a pan above roughly 200 °C rests on a thin cushion of steam, which conducts heat poorly and slows the flow of heat from the pan.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: contrast what happens on the two pans (seconds versus a minute or more) and explain why (a steam cushion that conducts heat poorly forms on the hotter pan). Only one choice includes the contrast and the explanation.
explanation.A: Correct. It contrasts the two pans and explains the difference with the poorly conducting steam cushion.
explanation.B: Incorrect. It states the contrast clearly but does not explain why it happens. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. It names and dates the effect but neither describes the contrast in detail nor explains it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. It explains what happens on the very hot pan but never contrasts it with a cooler pan.
